description.narrative:
Calculating ODA Eligibility:
53% of the tariff costs are counted as ODA eligible. This percentage was determined by breaking down the activities that the tariff was expected to fund, estimating the cost of each activity as a proportion of the total tariff value, and assessing whether each activity met ODA eligibility criteria. For example, support for arrivals (e.g. welcoming) is considered ODA eligible.
For thank you payments, the first year of payments is classified as ODA eligible as these fall under in-donor refugee assistance. Subsequent years are not ODA eligible, in line with the OECD DAC time limit which restricts in-donor refugee cost eligibility to the first 12 months of a refugee's stay.

The Homes for Ukraine scheme aims to provide safety and stability in the UK for individuals and families fleeing the war in Ukraine. The programme operates by matching Ukrainian nationals with UK-based sponsors who offer accommodation and broader support to help guests settle into life in the UK.
There are two primary types of funding available through the scheme:
Sponsor ‘Thank You’ Payment: A monthly optional payment of £350 is provided to sponsors as a gesture of appreciation from the UK Government for their generosity in hosting Ukrainian guests.
Local Authority Tariff: A one-off payment of £5,900 per guest is allocated to local authorities. This funding is intended to support the effective delivery of the scheme, including:
Conducting safeguarding and accommodation checks Administering sponsor payments Providing integration and resettlement support Preventing homelessness Assisting guests in accessing employment and the private rented sector (PRS)
This wraparound support ensures that Ukrainian guests receive the help they need to rebuild their lives in the UK.

The UK government launched the Homes for Ukraine scheme (the scheme) on 14 March 2022, following the Russian invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. The scheme enables people in the UK to act as sponsors for Ukrainian nationals and their families seeking refuge from the war.
